modules.title: 并发扣最后一件库存时，怎样保证整体结果？
这个案例怎样从失败变成可验收结果

items.title: 问题与关键机制
items.text: 两个请求同时读取最后一件库存时，分开的读取和扣减可能让两边都认为能成功；把检查和扣减作为一个不可分割的操作，只有仍满足条件的请求完成扣减，另一请求整体失败。

items.title: 怎样观察改善
items.text: 另一个请求应当明确失败并收到库存不足提示，不能产生第二张成功订单。最后核对库存、成功订单数和失败反馈是否彼此一致。

items.title: 领取客服工单也需要原子性
items.text: 两名客服同时领取同一工单时，检查“未领取”和写入负责人必须是一个原子操作；只能一人成功，另一人收到已被领取。

modules.title: 仍不保证什么
modules.text: 原子性只覆盖明确划定的操作范围；它并不代表支付、发货和其他分布式服务也能作为一个整体回滚。

lessonPractice.title: 库存只有 1 件，两个请求都读到了 1。哪种改法能保持结果正确？

options.label: 把库存条件检查和扣减放进一个不可分割的数据库操作
options.feedback: 对。检查通过的请求才能完成扣减，另一个请求会明确失败，库存不会被卖成两份。

options.label: 先让两个请求分别读取库存，再各自写入库存减一
options.feedback: 两个请求可能都基于旧值写入，页面看似成功但会产生两张订单或错误库存。

options.label: 在两个用户的页面上都禁用按钮，等待其中一个请求结束
options.feedback: 页面按钮状态不能限制另一个用户或重试请求，真正的并发保护必须在共享数据的一侧完成。

en.title: There is only 1 item in stock, and two requests both read 1. Which change keeps the result correct?

options.label: Combine the inventory condition check and deduction into one indivisible database operation
options.feedback: Correct. Only a request that passes the check completes the deduction; the other fails clearly instead of creating a second sale.

options.label: Let both requests read inventory first, then have each write inventory minus one
options.feedback: Both requests can write based on the stale value, producing two orders or an incorrect inventory result.

options.label: Disable the button on both users' pages and wait for one request to finish
options.feedback: A page button state cannot restrict another user or a retry; concurrency protection must be enforced where the shared data is updated.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请检查抢购流程：在库存为 1 时模拟两个请求同时到达，确保检查库存和扣减库存是一个不可分割的数据库操作。验收确认只能产生一个成功订单且库存变为 0，另一个请求收到库存不足；不要把前端禁用按钮当成并发保护。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Inspect the purchase flow: when inventory is 1, simulate two concurrent requests and make the inventory check and deduction one indivisible database operation. Verify that exactly one order succeeds, inventory becomes 0, and the other request receives out-of-stock; do not treat a disabled frontend button as concurrency protection.

learning.assumes: You know that multiple requests can change the same data at once.
learning.outcome: You can identify a check and update that must be indivisible and verify only one successful result.

modules.title: How can the final item stay correct under concurrent requests?
How the case moves from failure to a verifiable result

items.title: Problem and key mechanism
items.text: When two requests read the last item separately from deducting it, both may believe they can succeed; make the check and deduction one indivisible action so only the request that still meets the condition decrements stock and the other fails as a whole.

items.title: How to observe the improvement
items.text: The other request should fail completely with an out-of-stock response, without producing a second successful order. Then verify that remaining inventory, the successful order count, and the failure feedback all agree.

items.title: Claiming a support ticket also needs atomicity
items.text: When two agents claim the same ticket, checking that it is unassigned and assigning the owner must be one atomic operation. Only one agent succeeds; the other is told it was already claimed.

modules.title: What this still does not guarantee
modules.text: Atomicity covers only the defined scope of operations. It does not mean payment, shipping, or other distributed services across systems can roll back as one unit.

distinctions.label: Transaction
distinctions.text: {c:atomicity} emphasizes that operations cannot be split and intermediate states are never exposed; a {c:transaction} is the database container mechanism providing atomicity and isolation.

distinctions.label: Lock
distinctions.text: A {c:lock} is a mutual-exclusion mechanism for concurrent access; {c:atomicity} is the indivisible guarantee of the final result.
